chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from 'Ali ibn Sa'id, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a man who hired a donkey, then came with it to the cloth merchants and bought from them one garment or two garments, then left the donkey behind. He said: "The donkey is to be returned to its owner, and the one who went away with the two garments is to be pursued, but there is no hand-cutting upon him; it is only a betrayal."

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ الثِّيَابِ: the cloth merchants or sellers of garments
key_terms.الْحِمَارَ: the donkey that had been rented
key_terms.خِيَانَةٌ: betrayal of trust, not classified here as hadd-theft
key_terms.قَطْعٌ: the hadd punishment of hand-cutting for theft
key_terms.يُتْبَعُ: he is to be pursued or tracked down

ai.seo_question: When does taking property count as betrayal rather than theft in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling distinguishing betrayal of trust from theft that incurs the hadd punishment. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the hired donkey must be returned to its owner and the offender pursued for the garments, but the penalty of cutting does not apply because the act is classified as خِيَانَة rather than theft.
